evaluation_name: Stage 8B: Dynamic Control-Aware Fault Detection (Reconciled v2)

H8B.1_dynamic_vs_static.claim: Dynamic exogenous modeling improves R2 and normal residual stability over static Ridge.
H8B.1_dynamic_vs_static.reconciliation_verdict: Refuted: Dynamic exogenous lags improve training fit (+13.9% R2 on AHU9, +5.1% R2 on AHU10) but fail to generalize on the out-of-sample validation week (AHU9 val R2: 0.0512, AHU10 val R2: -12.7253) due to regime shift and lack of dynamic excitation.

H8B.2_controller_compensation_risk.claim: Controller-conditioned model risks explaining away control compensation through tracking error.
H8B.2_controller_compensation_risk.reconciliation_verdict: Confirmed on AHU-09 at matched FAR (~5%): M4 detects 15 rows (6 episodes) vs M5's 8 rows (3 episodes). On AHU-10, severe baseline shift caused tracking error to inadvertently act as an empirical drift filter.

H8B.3_regime_specific_fusion.claim: Regime-specific robust normalization controls false alarms across cooling and economizer modes within <=5% FAR budget.
H8B.3_regime_specific_fusion.reconciliation_verdict: M7 exhibits excessive false alarm rates (14.62% on AHU9, 18.94% on AHU10), heavily exceeding the <=5.0% operational FAR budget.

ahu9.verdict: At comparable FAR, M4 achieves 15 rows / 6 episodes vs M5's 8 rows / 3 episodes. Controller conditioning absorbs the alarm.

ahu10.verdict: On AHU-10, severe unmodeled seasonal drift penalized M4, whereas M5's tracking error inadvertently absorbed drift.

control_theory_closed_loop_audit.original_statement: High residual autocorrelation mathematically proves Kalman/N4SID impossibility.
control_theory_closed_loop_audit.corrected_scientific_statement: High autocorrelation of Ridge residuals (r1 > 0.91) demonstrates that the passive operational BMS data violates white-innovation and persistent excitation requirements for naive ARX and Ridge Kalman models. It does NOT mathematically prove that closed-loop identification is fundamentally impossible in control theory (which can succeed under deliberate dither or specialized closed-loop identification frameworks). It strictly demonstrates that the current passive dataset without active excitation is ill-conditioned for state-space identification.

ahu9.r2_discrepancy_explanation: Dynamic lag features improve training fit (AHU9: 0.4713 -> 0.6105; AHU10: 0.3443 -> 0.3951), but suffer from cross-regime validation overfitting under seasonal shifts (AHU9 val R2: 0.0512; AHU10 val R2: -12.7253). A typographical error (0.0518 -> 0.518) in the initial draft narrative was reconciled.
